source: md/1_PRD.md FR-27 (P0, PS A, line 206: '7-day appeal clock from decision upload; one appeal only; schedule SAC; record Council final decision'), the §7 rules table (line 288: 'Appeal to Council | Once, within 7 days of decision upload | 2.24a'), and §11 line 288 (the institution-side 'Speaking Order uploaded' cadence 'Day 3 and day 6 of 7; window closes day 7' — the two reminder days the appeal-clock sweep reuses). md/rules2.json REG-APPEAL-001 records the 7-day figure as an unverified example and explicitly instructs not to activate it as binding.
note: PLACEHOLDER CONFIG — the 7-day window and the one-appeal-only limit are AICTE regulatory values (APH cl. 2.24a). A human Executive Committee decision links its Speaking Order document, and this advisory clock uses that document's uploaded_at as its trigger. The endpoint only displays a countdown and a may-file flag; this configuration never gates a decision or rejects an appeal. Values remain Unverified/placeholder and must not be represented as binding until an official clause is confirmed (DEC-0003, REG-APPEAL-001).

trigger.note: For decisions with a linked Speaking Order, use the human-uploaded document time. Older decisions without a linked order retain their existing advisory state-entry timestamp. The seven-day duration remains a clearly labelled, nonbinding placeholder.

receiving_authority.label: State-level Advisory Committee (SAC) — scheduled after the appeal window
receiving_authority.note: FR-27 ends with 'schedule SAC; record Council final decision'. Which SAC, and who sits it, is an open human question (same class as the §19 Q5 designated authority); this names the role, never a person, and schedules nothing on its own.

reminder_thresholds.note: PRD §11 line 288 — first reminder, day 3 of the 7-day window.
PRD §11 line 288 — second reminder, day 6 of the 7-day window (the day before it closes).
